widgets_values:
SILENT OUTPUT CONTRACT. This workflow contains no external audio upload, audio trim, audio concatenation, decoded H3 audio, decoded LTX audio or final audio mux. The final CreateVideo audio socket is intentionally disconnected. LTX-2.5 and MiniMax H3 retain only their model-required internal joint-latent components; no audio is decoded, exposed or saved.

H3 DIVERSE PHYSICAL-FX CONTRACT. The five bridges must not share a dominant material, transition mechanism or silhouette. Pair 1 uses photoreal tunnel-perimeter explosions, practical debris, smoke and water pressure. Pair 2 uses one foreground camera-glass crack with true refraction and transparent shards. Pair 3 alone changes into a tactile 2D comic page with ink, halftone panels and a hand-torn paper reveal. Pair 4 uses analog 35mm emulsion blistering and chemical film burn. Pair 5 uses an exhaust shockwave, suspended water curtain, refracted droplets and spark-lit spray. Every bridge uses a hidden 15-frame motion-matching preroll, then delivers generated frames 16–39 as the exact 24-frame transition. Effects may dominate the middle but must preserve the actual previous LTX tail, avoid subject morphs and land sharply on the correct next supplied frame.

MASTER SPATIAL / TEMPORAL / AUDIO CONTRACT — LOCKED. Every loaded image, both LTX guide paths, the LTX latent, every H3 reference latent, every decoded segment and final assembly use exactly 1280×768. Both dimensions are divisible by 32; 1.5× delivery is exactly 1920×1152, also divisible by 32. H3 uses the same native 1280×768 canvas and a valid 39-frame 17k+5 generation grid; keep final 24 frames for exactly 1.00 second at the shared native 24fps. No 736→720 rescale, no hidden 720→704 VAE crop, no mixed 24/30fps assembly and no RIFE timebase conversion in the master.

MASTER CONTEXT POLICY. One global direction string is concatenated into all six LTX prompts, and every H3 prompt repeats the same color, identity, camera-momentum and no-reset rules in pair-specific form. A single model-agnostic conditioning tensor cannot be shared between LTX and H3 because their encoders and conditioning schemas differ; forcing one would be invalid. Cross-model continuity is therefore carried by the real decoded LTX tail frame plus the next supplied keyframe, while the common written contract keeps palette and editorial grammar consistent.

MASTER AUDIO POLICY. Eleven separately generated soundbeds would reset ambience and accumulate H3 audio-grid rounding at every seam. Upload one continuous master music/SFX file in LOAD MASTER AUDIO. It is trimmed once to the exact delivered duration: 558 frames / 24fps = 23.250000s, then muxed with the native 1280×768 master. LTX and H3 generated audio remains available on their own nodes for shot audition, but is deliberately not stitched into the final master.

DOPAMINE-MAX DIRECTION: every LTX scene delivers a new large-scale stunt, camera-axis change, shockwave, controlled jump, spark detonation, fire vortex or supernatural environmental event approximately every 0.35–0.50 seconds. Motion must be legible and continuous, not random flicker; car geometry, wheel contact and subject identity remain coherent. Every H3 bridge uses a completely different full-frame signature system and inherits the real preceding LTX tail velocity. H3 may reach maximum abstraction through its middle but must still transfer forward momentum and decisively land on the correct next reference. No two H3 bridges may share the same principal shapes, material, axis or reveal mechanism.

DYNAMIC CONTINUITY RULE: Each supplied Frame launches a three-second LTX shot with decisive camera travel, subject movement, parallax, evolving composition and no freeze or return-to-start loop. The real last generated image from each LTX Scene 1–5 is extracted at frame index 72 and becomes Picture 1 of its adjacent H3 bridge. Picture 2 of that H3 is the next supplied keyframe. The resulting sequence is moving LTX Scene 1 → momentum-matched H3 1→2 → moving LTX Scene 2, continuing through moving LTX Scene 6. H3 must inherit motion direction from the actual LTX tail and land on the next scene already in motion; it must never reset to or repeatedly recycle Frame 2.

SIX MANDATORY PHOTOGRAPHIC SCENES IN THIS EXACT LOADED-NODE ORDER: Frame 1 is the black sedan drifting through the wet purple fluorescent tunnel; Frame 2 is exactly two suited men shaking hands on the stormy rooftop with one briefcase and magenta fire; Frame 3 is the dark winged tuner car driving beneath a colossal violet lightning strike; Frame 4 is the wrecked coupe burning in an empty wet lot; Frame 5 is the dark rear-view tuner car firing twin purple exhaust flames; Frame 6 is the white modified coupe drifting beside a guardrail and throwing violet sparks. Do not reorder these six loaded images and do not infer order from their upload filenames.

TIMELINE ARCHITECTURE: every Frame receives its own independent LTX image-to-video shot using that same Frame as both its first and last anchor. H3 is used only between adjacent LTX shots: Frame 1→2, 2→3, 3→4, 4→5 and 5→6. Therefore every one of the six supplied images must appear as a full recognizable scene in the final video; no image may be used only as a hidden transition endpoint. Never let Frame 2 or any other single Frame dominate unrelated shots.

GLOBAL LOOK: photoreal nocturnal street-racing fever dream, deep indigo shadows, electric violet and hot magenta practical light, wet asphalt and concrete reflections, tactile 35mm grain, crisp subject geometry, controlled bloom and grounded physical motion. H3 styles must stay pair-specific and visibly different: fluorescent shutter geometry for 1→2, electrical contour drafting for 2→3, prismatic glass refraction for 3→4, liquid cel flame for 4→5, and long-exposure slit scan for 5→6. No readable text, logo, UI, franchise mark, invented crowd or generic replacement scene.
